newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end pedestrian day mildly firmer.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end pedestrian day mildly firmer.

text.p: * NZ share market firms in pedestrian trade
* National Mutual day's star after China news
* Market seen still chugging in same range next week
New Zealand's share market ended a pedestrian session mildly firmer and brokers predict the market will stride on in similar vein next week.
"The near-term outlook is pretty much the same. I can't see the market going too far from here," said Merrill Lynch broker Tim Koller.
He said results of the top two companies this week, Telecom and Carter Holt, did little to change perceptions.
The top 40 index closed 4.13 up at 2,314.84 on volume of $54 million.
Telecom dominated the volume with turnover of $21 million including a line of 1.7 million at $6.66. It ended up two at $6.64.
Brokers were uncertain whether the second stage of the company's $1 billion share buyback was underway or not. The company would not comment.

Highlight of the day was the 15 cent rise to to $2.29 of National Mutual. News that its parent Axa-UAP had been granted a licence to operate in China spurred the rise, although the company managing director Geoff Tomlinson told Reuters he urged caution about the news.

The Fletcher shares were mixed on news that the company employee trust had sold down its holding to 2.7 percent from 11.7 percent. Energy rose five cent to $4.70, Building four to $4.04 while Forest fell seven to $1.93.
Enerco was barely traded and unchanged on $5.85 after it reported an annual profit on expectations.

Northland Port rose three cents to $3.00 despite its first half profit falling 26.5 percent. Brokers said the news had been well flagged and investors took more note of its statement that it expects an improved second half.
